In The Court Of Ms. Ruby Neeraj Kumar,
Senior Civil Judge-Cum-Rent Controller,
South District, Saket Courts, New Delhi.

Smt. Veena Gupta
W/o Sh. Vikash Gupta

Jvts Garden, Chhatarpur Extension,
New Delhi.

3rd Floor, Jvts Garden,

Suit For Permanent & Mandatory Injunction. 
Date of institution of suit : 03.02.2018
Date of arguments : 27.05.2024 
Date of pronouncement of judgment : 29.05.2024
 Ex-Parte Judgment 
1. Vide this ex-parte judgment, I shall decide the present suit,
filed by the plaintiff against the defendant, for permanent &
mandatory injunction as well as miscellaneous application bearing no. 104/2018 under Order XXXIX Rule 2A r/w Section 151 CPC r/w Section 10 & 12 of the Contempt of Court Act,
filed by the plaintiff against the defendant. 
CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 1 /16  2. The relief sought by the plaintiff by way of present suit is reproduced as under:
 (a) Permanent Injunction with cost in favour  of the plaintiff and against the defendant, her  agents, servants, legal heirs, associates, attorneys,
 assignees, successors, administrators or any other  person on her behalf, thereby restraining them  from creating any hindrance and/or obstruction in Veena Gupta vs Myna Mukharjee on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162042048/
1  the supply of water of the plaintiff's flat on the  first floor of the property bearing No. C-33/1A,
 Khasra No. 967/2, JVTS Garden, Chhatarpur  Extension, New Delhi.
 (b) Mandatory Injunction with cost in favour of  the plaintiff and against the defendant, her agents,
 servants, legal heirs, associates, attorneys,
 assignees, successors, administrators or any other  person on her behalf, thereby directing the  defendant to remove her locks from the door of  the terrace and allow the plaintiff to go on the  terrace and have access to her overhead water  tank installed on the terrace of the property  bearing No. C-33/1A, Khasra No. 967/2, JVTS  Garden, Chhatarpur Extension, New Delhi. 
 (c) Mandatory Injunction with cost in favour of  the plaintiff and against the defendant, her agents,
 servants, legal heirs, associates, attorneys,
 assignees, successors, administrators or any other CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 2 /16  person on her behalf, thereby bearing No. C-  33/1A, Khasra No. 967/2, JVTS Garden,
 Chhatarpur Extension, New Delhi. 
Brief Facts 3. Facts of the case in nutshell as discernible from the plaint are that the plaintiff is absolute owner and in possession of the flat on first floor of the property bearing No. C-33/1A, Khasra No. 967/2,
JVTS Garden, Chhatarpur Extension, New Delhi, ad- measuring 250 square yards (hereinafter referred to as 'suit property'). It is averred that the defendant was the owner of a plot ad-measuring 250 square yards situated in the revenue area of village, Chhatarpur, New Delhi comprised in Khasra No. 967/2, which is now renowned as JVTS Garden, Chhatarpur Extension, New Delhi.
Defendant entered into a Collaboration Agreement with one R.P. Singh i.e. Builder/Developer and constructed/developed a building comprising of four floors, with one flat on each floor, on the said plot. Plaintiff had purchased the suit property, comprising of four bed rooms, one drawing- cum-dining room, one living room, one kitchen, two toilet-cum- bathroom alongwith one car parking at common parking area with all structure, fixtures, fittings, provisions, undivided &
indivisible ownership right in the land underneath, together with the right to use/avail common entrance and stairs, common safety tank, common underground water tank and separate water tank on the top floor of the building. 
4. It is averred that the defendant is residing on the third floor of the building. It is the case of the plaintiff that the defendant is CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 3 /16 harassing the Veena Gupta vs Myna Mukharjee on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162042048/
2 plaintiff & her family members, on one ground or the other i.e. by causing obstructions to the water supply of the plaintiff's flat, by putting lock on the door of the terrace etc. Several complaints have been made by the plaintiff against the defendant at PS Mehrauli but to no avail. It is averred that since September 2017, the defendant is trying to create third party interest in the common area of the building in question and with respect to the same, plaintiff has filed a separate suit for permanent injunction against the defendant, before this court. In the said suit, vide order dated 24.01.2018, application under Order XXXIX Rule 1 & 2 CPC was decided in favour of the plaintiff. 
The defendant got angry due to the same and stopped the supply of water to the plaintiff's flat by putting down the valve outside the overhead water tank, installed on the terrace of the building. It is further averred that there are two passages leading to the terrace of the building, one from inside the flat of the defendant and another passage is common for all the residents of the building, but the defendant is not allowing the plaintiff to go on the terrace to inspect her overhead water tank.
Defendant has also put her lock on the main gate of the terrace.
5. It is further averred that the water is stored in the overhead water tank through electric motor,
from the supply of water stored in common underground water tank and the plaintiff is regularly paying the charges with respect to the same to the JVTS Resident Welfare Society. It is further submitted that the plaintiff had previously signed a maintenance agreement executed between the plaintiff and the defendant under compelling circumstances. As per the said agreement, plaintiff was required CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 4 /16 to annually pay a sum of Rs.
60,000/- for the services mentioned in the agreement and Rs. 5,500/- towards the usage of lift installed in the building. It is further submitted that charges of the electric meter used for operation of electric motor for flow of water from underground water tank to overhead water tank were always paid in cash, separately by the plaintiff and the same is evident from the fact that on the electricity bill issued by BSES dated 06.04.2017, defendant has given a written acknowledgment qua receipt of cheque bearing No. 000019 dated 10.06.2017 of Rs. 2,157/- as 1/3rd share towards the charges of electric motor installed on the ground floor. It is submitted that the defendant did not provide the details of the expenses incurred towards the maintenance and misused the said money of the plaintiff and therefore, plaintiff did not renew the said maintenance agreement. 
6. It is further submitted that due to the acts of the defendant, plaintiff has been constrained to arrange water for cooking food, drinking and cleanliness purposes, on day-to-day basis from outside sources, which is causing great harassment to the plaintiff and her family members. Hence, the present suit has been filed. 
7. Summons of the suit were duly served upon the defendant. The defendant entered appearance and filed the WS refuting the submissions made by the plaintiff. It is submitted by the defendant that the suit of the plaintiff revolves around the maintenance agreement, which has been filed and relied upon by the plaintiff. It is further submitted that as per the said maintenance agreement,
plaintiff has failed to clear the maintenance charges due to which defendant had also issued a CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 5 /16 legal notice dated 16.01.2018 to the plaintiff,
demanding the arrears of maintenance to the tune of Rs. 65,500/-. It is further submitted that the suit property is situated in an unregularized area and there is no supply of water by government aided agencies like Delhi Jal Board and it is the defendant, who is arranging the water supply Veena Gupta vs Myna Mukharjee on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162042048/
3 through water tank as well as other sources with concerned authorities, in lieu of the maintenance agreement duly executed between the parties. It is averred that the defendant has paid all the expenses for getting the pipeline installed in the said building and there is one electric motor, which runs the water throughout the building and gives uninterrupted supply of water to the residents throughout the day. It is further submitted that the water is stored in the overhead tanks as JVTS supplies water only for a limited time period of one hour and it is the defendant, who stores the water in the underground tank situated at the ground floor and the same is stored at the overhead water tank through electric motor. It is submitted that the plaintiff has failed to pay the maintenance charges of about Rs. 2 lacs and the present suit has been filed with a motive to avoid making the payment of said charges. 
8. It is pertinent to mention herein that no replication was filed by the plaintiff to the WS of the defendant. 
9. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed by the Ld.
Predecessor vide order dated 29.07.2019. 
Issues 1. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to relief of permanent injunction as prayed for ? OPP CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 6 /16 2. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to relief of mandatory injunction as prayed for? OPP 3. Whether the plaintiff is liable to pay maintenance dues as alleged in the written statement? OPD 4. Whether the suit is liable to be dismissed on ground of absence of cause of action or locus standi or suppression of material facts? OPD 5. Relief. 
Plaintiff's Evidence 10. In ex-parte plaintiff's evidence, Veena Gupta i.e. plaintiff was examined as PW-1 and her affidavit in evidence was tendered, which is Ex.PW-1/A. In support of her case, plaintiff has relied upon the following documents:
(a) Ex. PW-1/1, which is Agreement to sell dated 02.02.2017.
(b) Ex. PW-1/2, which is GPA, Affidavit, Will, Possession Letter, Receipt, all dated 01.10.2016.
(c) Ex. PW-1/3 , which is Maintenance Agreement.
Veena Gupta vs Myna Mukharjee on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162042048/
4 (d) Ex. PW-1/4, which is BSES Bill dated 06.04.2017. 
(e) Ex. PW-1/5 (colly.), which is copy of complaints dated 11.06.2017, 14.01.2018 & 31.01.2018. 
(f) Ex. PW-1/6, which is copy of e-mail.
11. Defendant failed to appear and cross-examine PW-1 and therefore, defendant was proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 20.12.2019. 
CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 7 /16 Ex-parte Arguments 12. I have heard the final arguments advanced by learned counsel for the plaintiff and carefully perused the record. 
13. Ld. Counsel for the plaintiff has argued that the defendant has been proceeded ex-parte and therefore, case of the plaintiff stands proved by virtue of unchallenged & uncontroverted evidence. 
He has prayed that the suit of the plaintiff be decreed accordingly. 
Findings 14. I have heard the final arguments advanced by learned counsel for the plaintiff and carefully perused the record. Though, no evidence has been led by the defendants, however, issues were framed by the Ld. Predecessor vide order dated 29.07.2019. Thus, issue-wise findings of this Court are as under:-
Issue No. 1: Whether the plaintiff is entitled to relief of permanent injunction as prayed for ? OPP AND Issue No. 3: Whether the plaintiff is liable to pay maintenance dues as alleged in the written statement? OPD 15. Issue no.1 & 2. are taken up together as they are intermeshed and discussion on one issue would affect the other issue. In the instant case, the first relief sought by the plaintiff is to restrain the defendant & her agents, associates etc. from creating any hindrance and/or obstruction in the supply of water of the suit property. It is alleged by the plaintiff that the CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 8 /16 defendant no.1 has stopped the supply of water to the plaintiff's flat by putting down the valve outside the overhead water tank, installed on the terrace of the building. On the contrary, defendant has claimed that the plaintiff has not paid the maintenance charges as per the maintenance agreement, executed between them in October, 2016. 
The entire issue, as rightly stated by the defendant in the Written Statement, revolves around the said maintenance agreement, which is admitted by both the parties. The relevant terms of the maintenance agreement are reproduced as under: -
Veena Gupta vs Myna Mukharjee on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162042048/
5 " 7. The SECOND PARTY shall pay the maintenance charges to FIRST PARTY, at flat rate of Rs. 5000/- per month in advance annually every year and Rs. 5500/- per year towards the lift. The annual maintenance charges will be subject to revision with an expected enhanced minimum based on actual expenses incurred after completing every 1 year on the last rate. Costs for annual polishing or painting of the exterior are not be covered in the maintenance charges and will proportionately split on an actual cost basis. 
9. The SECOND PARTY shall also pay additionally, all charges related to electricity consumed by the SECOND PARTY for the common areas to the FIRST PARTY or to the local Electric supply authority, as per directions of the FIRST PARTY. 
10. The SECOND PARTY shall also pay proportionate share of water consumption charges for the moor pump as may be billed by local concerned authority to the FIRST PARTY. 
16. It is evident from the maintenance agreement that the plaintiff is bound to pay the maintenance charges of Rs 5,000/- per month, in advance annually, every year &
Rs.5,500 per year, towards the lift, to the defendant and in addition to the same,
plaintiff is required to pay all charges related to electricity consumed by the defendant for the common areas of the building CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs.
Myna Mukharjee 9 /16 & proportionate share of water consumption charges for the motor pump. 
17. The first assertion of the plaintiff in support of her case is that she has paid the maintenance charges for one year as evident from the receiving given by the defendant on the electricity bill. Secondly, she has claimed that the defendant did not provide the details of the expenses incurred towards the maintenance and misused the said money of the plaintiff & therefore, plaintiff did not renew the said maintenance agreement. With respect to the proof of regular payment of the maintenance charges, plaintiff has merely adduced electricity bill dated 6.04.2017,
which bears the receiving of Rs. 2,157 towards 1/3 rd share of the total bill. No other document or evidence has been adduced by the plaintiff to show that she has been regularly paying the maintenance charges to the defendant as per the maintenance agreement. Other than pleading vaguely, the plainti ought to have placed something on record showing that she had been regularly paying the maintenance charges. 
Further, the assertion of the plaintiff that the defendant did not provide the details of the expenses incurred towards the maintenance, does not inspire confidence of this court as the defendant has claimed to have sent legal demand notice dated 16.01.2018 to the plaintiff to that effect. The copy of said legal notice, though not been proved by the defendant, has been placed on record and the plaintiff has not denied the same by filing replication. 
Veena Gupta vs Myna Mukharjee on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162042048/
6 18. The question that arises at this juncture is whether the plaintiff is entitled to equitable relief of injunction without having proved on record, the payment of maintenance charges as CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 10 /16 per the maintenance agreement. The law is well settled with regard to the relief of injunction that one who seeks equity must do equity and one who seeks equity must come with clean hands. If a party is found to be on the wrong side of law by its own acts and omissions, it cannot cry foul. The Court is duty bound to strictly deal with litigations based on facts, which have either been misrepresented or distorted to suit the convenience of a litigant. In the case at hand, the maintenance agreement,
executed between the parties is an admitted document and it requires the plaintiff to pay the maintenance charges for availing the services, mentioned therein. The plaintiff has made contradictory submissions in single breadth by claiming on one hand that she has rescinded from the maintenance agreement and on the other hand that the defendant has not told her the maintenance charges, due & payable for the services availed. However, both the submissions lead to the only conclusion that the plaintiff has not paid the maintenance charges as required by the maintenance agreement. She has further stated that she is still ready to pay the proportionate amount of the electricity charges & the lift services but even her expressed willingness to pay the proportionate amount of the electricity charges & the lift services is nothing but a sham because, if she had any intention to pay the same, she could have made the said payment before the court. Plaintiff herself being in the wrong, is not entitled to claim any equitable relief from the court. 
19. Further, plaintiff has asserted that she had signed the maintenance agreement under compelling circumstances and she did not renew it as the defendant was misusing her money. The CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 11 /16 said assertions are totally baseless & and not supported by any evidence. Plaintiff has not bothered to explain as to what were the compelling circumstances, which led her to sign the maintenance agreement or how the defendant was misusing the maintenance charges. Pleading, which is not supported with cogent & substantial evidence is vain. Another argument of the plaintiff that she had not renewed the said maintenance agreement and therefore, she is not liable to pay the maintenance charges, also does not sustain as the plaintiff admittedly did not forego all the facilities provided to her under the maintenance agreement. Plaintiff can not be permitted under law to accept only some terms of the maintenance agreement and deny the others, as per her own wish unless, there is such clause in the agreement it self. There is evidently, no such clause in the maintenance agreement. In view of the aforesaid discussion, it would not be erroneous to hold that the present suit appears to have been filed by the plaintiff to avoid making the payment of the maintenance charges to the defendant as per the maintenance agreement. Thus issue no.1 & 3 are decided against the plaintiff and in favor of the defendant. However, it is clarified that this court is not giving any finding on the quantum of maintenance charges to be paid by the plaintiff as the present suit does not call for the same. 
Veena Gupta vs Myna Mukharjee on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162042048/
7 Issue no. 2: Whether the plaintiff is entitled to relief of mandatory injunction as prayed for? OPP 20. The relief of mandatory injunction sought by the plaintiff is twofold. Firstly,
directing the defendant to remove her locks from the door of the terrace and allow the plaintiff to go on the CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 12 /16 terrace & have access to her overhead water tank, installed on the terrace of the suit property. Secondly, directing the defendant to immediately restore the supply of water from the overhead water tank installed on the terrace of the property. 
21. As far as the second part of the mandatory injunction relief is concerned, it gets declined on the same reasoning and discussion as stated above. However, as regard the relief, directing the defendant to remove her locks from the door of the terrace and allow the plaintiff to go on the terrace & have access to her overhead water tank,
plaintiff has been able to show through the Agreement to Sell that she has the right to use/avail common entrance and stairs, common water tank, common septic tank without the right of terrace except for installation/maintain and separate water tank,
the TV antenna, staircase, passage and all other common facilities provided in the building. The defendant has not disputed the said agreement to sell but claim to have exclusive right to the terrace. Irrespective of the asserted right/ title of the defendant to the terrace, plaintiff has right to access the terrace for the limited purpose of installation/ maintenance of the water tank. In view of the same, issue no.2 is partly decided in the favor of the plaintiff and against the defendant. 
Issue No. 4: Whether the suit is liable to be dismissed on ground of absence of cause of action or locus standi or suppression of material facts? OPD 22. This issue was required to be proved by the defendant. However, in the absence of any evidence adduced, defendant has CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 13 /16 filed to prove the same. Thus this issue is decided against the defendant. 
APPLICATION UNDER ORDER XXXIX RULE 2A 23. By way of application under Order XXXIX Rule 2A, plaintiff has alleged that the defendant has committed the breach of order dated 03.02.2018, passed by the learned Predecessor and therefore, he is liable to be punished as per the law. Vide ex-parte order dated order dated 03.02.2018, Ld. Predecessor had directed the defendant to restore the water supply of the flat of the plaintiff. the relevant portion of the said order is reproduced as under:
" In view of the fact that the water supply is the basic amenity and it should not be withheld without any just cause, defendant is directed to restore water supply to the flat of plaintiff i.e.first floor of suit property no. C33/1A, Khasra no. 967/2, JVTS Veena Gupta vs Myna Mukharjee on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162042048/ 
8 Garden, Chattarpur Extension, New Delhi within 24 hours of the date of service of this order, till the next date of hearing"
24. It is alleged by the plaintiff that pursuant to the directions given by the Court vide Order dated 03.02.2018, the defendant had restored the water supply of the plaintiff's flat, however, on 30.08.2018, defendant in utter disobedience of the said order, stopped the water supply of the plaintiff's flat and also cut down all the wires installed for operating the electric motor for filling the overhead water tank and has also closed the valves of the overhead water tank so that water is not filled in the overhead water tank. 
25. Having gone through the record, I am of the opinion that there is no disobedience of the order dated 03.02.2018 by the defendant as vide the said order, he was only directed to restore CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 14 /16 the water supply of the plaintiff's flat, which as per the submission made by the plaintiff herself, was complied with by the defendant. The order restraining the defendant to create any hindrance or obstruction in the water supply to the plaintiff's flat was specifically passed on 29.07.2019.
26. Moreover, plaintiff has not placed any photograph or adduced any witness on record, in support of the said allegation. The provision under Order XXXIX Rule 2A CPC has penal consequence &
therefore, it cannot be invoked at the bare & groundless submission of the plaintiff when already they are at logger heads with each other. To invoke a penal provision, there has to be something more than a bald allegation. In view of the same, I am of the view that the application under Order XXXIX rule 2A is without any merit and therefore, stands dismissed. 
Relief 27. Accordingly, suit is partly decreed in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant, to the effect that the defendant is directed to allow the plaintiff to access the terrace of the suit property,
for the purpose of maintenance/installation of water tank. With respect to all other reliefs sought,
suit stands dismissed. 
28. No order as to costs. Decree sheet be prepared accordingly.

annotations.text: The law is well settled with regard to the relief of injunction that one who seeks equity must do equity and one who seeks equity must come with clean hands.
If a party is found to be on the wrong side of law by its own acts and omissions, it cannot cry foul.
The Court is duty bound to strictly deal with litigations based on facts, which have either been misrepresented or distorted to suit the convenience of a litigant.

In the case at hand, the maintenance agreement,
executed between the parties is an admitted document and it requires the plaintiff to pay the maintenance charges for availing the services, mentioned therein.

The plaintiff has made contradictory submissions in single breadth by claiming on one hand that she has rescinded from the maintenance agreement and on the other hand that the defendant has not told her the maintenance charges, due & payable for the services availed.
However, both the submissions lead to the only conclusion that the plaintiff has not paid the maintenance charges as required by the maintenance agreement.

She has further stated that she is still ready to pay the proportionate amount of the electricity charges & the lift services but even her expressed willingness to pay the proportionate amount of the electricity charges & the lift services is nothing but a sham because, if she had any intention to pay the same, she could have made the said payment before the court.
